title: Power Rankings: Spurs take over top spot
heading: 2011-12 Power Rankings: Week 15
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: No other team has won more than nine straight games this season. The Spurs? They're on their SECOND 11-game win streak of 2011-12. As Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News noted on Twitter, new Spur Boris Diaw has seen more wins since March 23 (10) than his old team (Charlotte) has all season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Should Miami finishing with the East's top seed -- in a season where Derrick Rose has missed almost a third of his team's games -- be a prerequisite for LeBron James to win the MVP trophy? Full disclosure: That's the way this voter is leaning as we enter the final two weeks and change before ballots are due to be turned in.

rankings.summaryHtml: So they've manufactured 15 wins (in 22 games) without D-Rose in the lineup and have about 20 days to go until the playoffs start to get the NBA's reigning MVP back to peak form. As long as there are no further health setbacks in a season filled with them, something tells me Chicago can live with those sorts of numbers.

rankings.summaryHtml: Only one team in the entire NBA knows how it feels to win road games in both OKC and Miami ... and both breakthroughs happened last week. You have to figure Z-Bo will be starting by the time the playoffs start, but that Grizz bench suddenly has a lot of firepower on it if Arenas keeps throwing in badly needed 3s.

rankings.summaryHtml: Seems like forever ago now that the Celts lost five straight to limp into the All-Star break. Ray Allen is figuring out his new bench gig, Rajon Rondo has topped 10 assists in 17 consecutive games and Boston is 17-7 since the break, good for a three-game Atlantic lead (and the No. 4 seed that goes with it) with 10 to go.

rankings.summaryHtml: If we're busting on all the top contenders (Spurs aside) for their collective inability to build up a head of steam as the playoffs approach, it's only right to point out that the Pacers jumped out to a 4-0 start in April before the Celts -- having dropped three of the teams' previous four meetings -- put the clamps on 'em.

rankings.summaryHtml: You can forgive a loss to the Lakers when it's the only loss in a span of nine games in the wake of my man Chris Broussard's report that Vinny Del Negro had lost his locker room. You can also start to look at the Clips as a real playoff factor if Randy Foye keeps making shots like he has for the past 10 or so games.

rankings.summaryHtml: As long as this shin thing doesn't linger, and as long as Bynum strays no further from the team's epicenter, I'd argue that the injury responsible for KO-ing Kobe from L.A.'s visit to Phoenix is actually a good thing. Impressive as a minutes title would be in No. 24's 16th season, there's no harm in some enforced rest.

rankings.summaryHtml: Goran Dragic is your new Western Conference player of the week. Courtney Lee has five 20-point games since becoming a starter on March 13. And Kyle Lowry is suddenly back from his bacterial infection. Might be tricky in the short term to find PT for all three, but Lowry is a trade asset now as long as Dragic re-signs.

rankings.summaryHtml: Quite an Easter Sunday for the Knicks. Spoiled D-Rose's return, moved to 11-3 (8-0 at home) under Woody, generated Melo's happiest headlines in months and even coaxed the reclusive Larry Johnson back to the organization to get some of that 1999 Finals mojo in the fold from the last lockout-shortened season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Where do you have Atlanta when you're drawing up your list of threats to the Chicago-Miami duopoly in the East? In a playoff series, I'd be inclined to put the Celts and Knicks at the top of the list. But perhaps this week's stops in Boston and Orlando give the Hawks two prime opportunities to change our minds.

rankings.summaryHtml: Silly me: Always assumed finishing in the lottery and getting lucky in the draft was central to the Suns' strategy to try to convince Steve Nash to stay. Yet I think I speak for neutrals everywhere (even if you don't think I'm neutral) that seeing Nash and the resurrected Michael Redd in the playoffs would be a treat for us all.

rankings.summaryHtml: If only divorcing Odom solved all of the champs' problems. They were down to No. 7 in the West as of Monday morning thanks to an offense still sputtering beyond recognition -- bordering on unwatchable when J-Kidd is out -- and 9-11 in the games (five points or less) so relished in Carlisle's first three seasons (55-22).

rankings.summaryHtml: There are realistically 19 teams still alive for 16 playoff slots. None of those 19 has a worse road record than Utah's 9-20 mark outside of SLC. So with four of the next six on the road, Utah surely won't protest if Pop decides Monday is one of those nights Tony, Timmy or Manu (or more than one) needs a night off.

rankings.summaryHtml: Dwight Howard's decision to relinquish his right to opt out of his contract at season's end was supposed to bring peace to the Magic Kingdom for the rest of this season at the very least. How long did the happiness last? Thanks to Stan Van Gundy's shootaround candor, here's your answer: Not even a month.

rankings.summaryHtml: Although its 13-4 surge since March 9 shines a significant spotlight on the Knicks' visit Wednesday to Brewtown, Milwaukee sees what we all see. Philadelphia, more so than New York, is truly the team that the Bucks are chasing after winning seven of their past road games and averaging nearly 109 ppg in that stretch.

rankings.summaryHtml: Professor Hollinger has made me a point-differential believer over the years, but the reeling, offensively challenged Sixers are doing everything they can to diminish the value of that stat. Despite going 9-18 since its glorious 20-9 start, Philly remains No. 5 in the league in that category with an average nightly margin of plus-4.4.

rankings.summaryHtml: Professor Hollinger has apparently taken to calling them the "Trail Tankers." I was actually going to question their commitment to tanking after that spirited comeback Friday night in Dallas to beat the reigning champs in OT, but 9-14 since the All-Star break seems defensible with the Nets' first-rounder on the way.

rankings.summaryHtml: K-Love is bidding to become the first player to average at least 26 and 13 since Shaq did it in his MVP season of 1999-2000, but that's about all that the injury-tortured Wolves have left to play for now. They're 4-12 without Rubio, which begs the question: How many of those 16 Rubio-free games have you watched?

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: Lawrence Frank's Pistons can actually claim to be better than .500 since their dreadful 4-20 start with a passable mark of 17-15 from Feb. 3 onwards. The bad news: Nearly a third of Detroit's 35 losses -- 11! -- have come by 20 points or more. Which is second-most in the NBA behind (gulp) only Charlotte.

rankings.summaryHtml: Beating Minnesota wasn't ideal, but the Dubs are generally tanking in the proper spirit. They're 3-12 since trading Monta and just started three rookies (Klay Thompson, Charles Jenkins and Jeremy Tyler) in five straight games for the first time since March of 1981 (Larry Smith, Joe Barry Carroll and Lorenzo Romar).

rankings.summaryHtml: You don't have to wait for adidas commercials to see Eric Gordon any more: He's back on the floor for the first time since early January to let everyone see that his knee is fully operational before free agency arrives. The flip side: New Orleans announced Monday morning that Jarrett Jack's season is over (stress fracture).

rankings.summaryHtml: It was a 21-point home win over Philly on March 30, against a team that has pounded on sub-.500 opposition all season, that really thrust Philly into its current funk. Unfortunately for the Wiz, that's probably a top-three highlight of their season. Open to suggestions from our Wiz faithful on the list of what trumps it.

rankings.summaryHtml: When the Bobs recorded their seventh W on March 17 in the 43rd game of the season, I figured they were safe from further comparisons to the '72-73 Sixers and locks to finish with a higher winning percentage than the worst team of all time's hideous .110 mark. Eleven straight L's later, all I can say is: What was I thinking?
